item.text: {"decision":"The newly completed evidence coverage does not change the main physical judgments: occurrence of V17/C17 support-fluid loss and sufficient vertical withdrawal remains supported, but keeper-bypass lateral/rotation/deformation path remains unresolved; V17 later seat contamination remains a plausible but unproven event-time leakage origin. The full joint fall mechanism therefore remains unresolved because the required keeper-bypass condition is still unmeasured.","operations":[{"action":"revise","expected_version":2,"replaces":null,"reason":"Reaffirmed after R_R3InspectionPhotos v5. D02.S05 requires lateral offset and dynamic-path evidence in addition to primary seating loss. D07.S03 reports release at 13:24:03 but says keeper-to-yoke interface and lateral offset were occluded and the clip cannot distinguish transient offset, rotation, or local deformation. D10.S02-S03 reports 8 +/- 1 mm centered seated keeper overlap and no simple vertical passage under rigid centered geometry, but says incident lateral offset/release rotation were not measured and no approved off-center dynamic retention envelope is available. D14.S01-S03 reports keeper plate/fasteners remained attached with no gross separation/fracture, but does not establish dynamic overlap; unmeasured deformation and off-center release path remain separate. D05.S02/D07.S02/D14.S02 support carrier-post/spreader contact visibility/marks, but not mark-specific dating, load, or bypass geometry. Thus the event keeper-bypass path remains unresolved, not refuted; reopening requires time-relevant lateral/rotation data, validated off-center dynamic retention-envelope analysis, or deformation/NDE evidence tied to the release path.","record":{"id":"N_R3KeeperBypassUnresolved","kind":"node","scope_key":"r3_keeper_bypass_lateral_offset_dynamic_path_event","claim":"During the R3 event, the carrier beam followed a lateral offset and dynamic path that bypassed keeper retention after any loss of primary seating engagement.","status":"unresolved","sources":["D02","D05","D07","D10","D14"],"depends_on":["R_R3InspectionPhotos","R_R3MotionRecord"],"from_ids":[],"to_id":null,"mode":null,"asset":null,"window":null,"fields":[]}},{"action":"revise","expected_version":2,"replaces":null,"reason":"Reaffirmed after R_R3InspectionPhotos v5. The edge requires all three premises jointly. D07/D08 continue to support about 40 mm relative withdrawal, exceeding D02.S05's 30 mm primary seating engagement, and D05/D08 support no independent positive block. However, D07.S03 occludes the keeper interface and lateral offset during release; D10.S03 says incident offset/rotation were not measured and no approved off-center dynamic retention envelope is available; D14.S01-S03 do not establish dynamic overlap and leave unmeasured deformation/off-center path separate. Because keeper-bypass remains unresolved, the full joint causal contribution from hydraulic withdrawal plus keeper bypass plus no block to the fall remains unresolved, although hydraulic withdrawal and no block remain compatible contributors.","record":{"id":"E_R3HydraulicWithdrawalKeeperBypassToFall","kind":"edge","scope_key":"r3_joint_hydraulic_withdrawal_keeper_bypass_no_block_caused_fall","claim":"Hydraulic support loss with sufficient relative yoke withdrawal, keeper-bypass dynamic path, and absence of positive mechanical restraint jointly caused or allowed the R3 delivery carrier beam fall.","status":"unresolved","sources":["D01","D02","D05","D07","D08","D10","D14"],"depends_on":[],"from_ids":["N_R3HydraulicWithdrawalUnresolved","N_R3KeeperBypassUnresolved","N_R3ActualBlockAbsentUnresolved"],"to_id":"N_FocalEvent_R3BeamFall","mode":"all","asset":null,"window":null,"fields":[]}},{"action":"revise","expected_version":1,"replaces":null,"reason":"Reaffirmed after R_R3V17LeakOriginRecords v2. D09.S02 later found V17 reverse leakage of 17 +/- 2 mL/min with CLOSED indication and later seat contamination; over 24 minutes, 17 mL/min gives about 408 mL, compatible with D08.S02's 0.400 +/- 0.010 L event flow. But D09.S01 says custody supports identity, not a timestamp for every defect; D09.S02 says contamination arrival time is unknown; D09.S03 says the later test alone does not establish the earlier leakage rate or when contamination developed; D08.S04 says the event meter does not establish valve wear age or contamination. D13.S01 only proposes V17 replacement, and D13.S02-S03 say implementation/effectiveness and defect cause are not documented. Therefore event-time seat contamination as the cause or rate controller of incident leakage remains unresolved, not supported or refuted. Reopening requires pre-event maintenance/leak-test history, contaminant identification/timing, fluid cleanliness/debris records, preservation/lab notes, or repair/teardown cause analysis.","record":{"id":"N_R3V17SeatContaminationEventTimingUnresolved","kind":"node","scope_key":"r3_v17_seat_contamination_present_during_event_and_caused_leakage","claim":"Seat contamination later found in V17 was already present during the 13:00-13:24 event interval and caused or controlled the incident V17 internal leakage.","status":"unresolved","sources":["D08","D09","D13"],"depends_on":["R_R3HydraulicRecords","R_R3V17LeakOriginRecords"],"from_ids":[],"to_id":null,"mode":null,"asset":null,"window":null,"fields":[]}}],"next_work":[],"upstream_dispositions":[],"disposition":"partial"}
